newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Ukraine to deliver 1.5 mln tonnes coal to Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to deliver 1.5 mln tonnes coal to Bulgaria.

text.p: Bulgaria, poor in energy resources and hamstrung by a lack of cash, has agreed to import 1.5 million tonnes of coal from Ukraine in 1997, the Energy Ministry said on Monday.
The coal, contracted at the end of last week, will be supplied for the 1,260-megawatt Varna coal and gas-fired plant, a ministry statement said.
It said the supplies would be paid in dollars and the prices and delivery terms would be fixed in contracts which would be signed between commercial organisations of the two countries.
Ukraine, Bulgaria's traditional supplier of high quality coal, raised prices of its patchy coal deliveries at the start of 1995 and Sofia was forced to halt imports last year.
The Varna plant that has traditionally used only Ukraine's Donbass coal has been idle since 1995.
Bulgaria, which produces mainly lignite, has also contracted 700,000 tonnes of coal from Vietnam.
The Varna plant is expected to help replace electricity production from the closed 440-megawatt nuclear reactor at Kozloduy.
Kozloduy's oldest Soviet-made reactor was closed in May for analysis of its vessel's metal amid international concern over its safety.
If the results of the analysis, expected in mid-November, do not permit the reactor to be restarted, the country will be forced to ration electricity supplies, energy officials say.
In July, the European Union said it would grant 10 million Ecus to Bulgaria's energy sector as compensation for the closure of the controversial reactor and the purchase of coal for the Varna plant.
Energy officials said last week the EU would grant another seven million Ecus to help Bulgaria buy more coal for the coming winter and thus try to avoid power cuts.
